title: Designing your pancreas DREADD experiment
objective: Assemble the pieces — Cre line, Cre-dependent AAV-DREADD, actuator, controls, readout — into a coherent pancreas experiment, using the colon paper as the template.

steps.title: The template you're copying
steps.body: The Wolfson/Ginty 2023 colon paper defined organ-innervating [[DRG]] subtypes, then manipulated them (optogenetics, ablation) to prove function. Your project swaps the readout organ to the **pancreas** and the manipulation to **[[DREADD|DREADDs]]**. Same logic: define the neurons → deliver a [[Cre]]-dependent tool → manipulate → measure.

flag.note: Exact pancreas-innervating DRG subtypes/levels are less established than the colon's — confirm with the lab and primary literature.

steps.title: Cre-dependent delivery: DIO/FLEX
steps.body: You put the DREADD behind a **Cre-dependent switch** so only your Cre+ neurons express it. The viral version is written **[[AAV]]-[[DIO]]-[[hM3Dq]]** (or -[[hM4Di]]) — 'DIO/FLEX' = double-[[loxP|floxed]] inverted ORF, flipped into the sense orientation only by Cre. Inject the AAV so it reaches pancreas-innervating sensory neurons, in a mouse whose Cre marks those neurons.

steps.prompt: Put the experiment in a sensible order.
items: Choose a Cre line that marks pancreas-innervating sensory neurons
Inject Cre-dependent AAV-DIO-DREADD to target those neurons
Wait for expression; confirm it's in the right cells (reporter)
Run a manipulation check (recording/c-Fos) that the DREADD works
Give actuator vs. vehicle with the needed control groups
steps.explanation: Specificity (Cre + Cre-dependent virus) is set before you ever give a drug; validation precedes interpretation.

steps.prompt: Your Cre line also labels some non-sensory cells near the pancreas. What's the cleanest fix, given the lab's toolkit?
options: Give a considerably larger dose of the actuator drug
Use Cre+Flp intersection so only sensory pancreas neurons get it
Ignore it, since those extra labeled cells probably don't matter
Switch the DREADD payload from hM3Dq over to hM4Di
steps.explanation: This is the specificity problem from C3. An intersection (e.g., a sensory-neuron [[Flp]] driver AND your Cre) restricts expression to the cells you actually mean. A [[retrograde]] AAV from the pancreas can add anatomical specificity too.

variants.setup: Your Cre line also labels some non-sensory cells near the pancreas.
variants.prompt: What's the cleanest fix, given the lab's toolkit?
options: Give a considerably larger dose of the actuator drug
Use Cre+Flp intersection so only sensory pancreas neurons get it
Ignore it, since those extra labeled cells probably don't matter
Switch the DREADD payload from hM3Dq over to hM4Di
variants.reveal: An intersection restricts expression to cells with both drivers, excluding the off-target non-sensory cells.

steps.scenario: After injection, your [[reporter]] shows DREADD expression is sparse and weak in the target neurons.
steps.prompt: Which is the LEAST likely culprit to check first?
options: AAV serotype/tropism not ideal for these neurons
Titer too low or too little volume delivered
Not enough time for expression before testing
The actuator was the wrong one
steps.explanation: Expression level is set before any [[actuator]] is given — [[serotype]], titer/volume, and expression time are the usual suspects. Actuator choice affects whether the DREADD fires, not how much DREADD is present.
steps.followUp: Revisit serotype (retrograde vs. local), titer, injection coordinates/volume, and the expression interval.

steps.setup: You silence pancreas-innervating sensory neurons (hM4Di + actuator) during a glucose tolerance test, with all control groups in place.
steps.prompt: What's the honest set of outcomes to prepare for?
options: Only a clearly positive result is even possible in this design
Glucose handling could change, not change, or shift in a subset
The mice will simply not survive the manipulation at all
The actuator guarantees that you will see a real effect
steps.reveal: With a confirmed manipulation and proper controls, any outcome is interpretable: an effect supports a role; a validated null says these neurons aren't necessary for this readout under these conditions. That's a real result, not a failure — which is why the manipulation check in L4 matters so much.

variants.prompt: Before silencing pancreas-innervating sensory neurons during a glucose tolerance test, what's the honest set of outcomes to prepare for?
options: Only a clearly positive result is even possible in this design
Glucose handling could change, not change, or shift in a subset
The mice will simply not survive the manipulation at all
The actuator guarantees that you will see a real effect
variants.explanation: Good design anticipates every outcome; a well-controlled null result is still a real finding.
